title: Redwood Discovery - SolsticePay latency & throughput

Share SOC2 & network diagram + KMS FAQ
Schedule 1-week performance POC for p95/throughput benchmarks w/ test corpus
action_items: Jamie: Email Dedicated pricing sheet and sample config (due: 2026-09-09)
Ravi: Prepare throughput benchmark plan and token/sec targets for POC (due: 2026-09-14)
Priya: Provide security questionnaire answers and required network constraints (due: 2026-09-10)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (SolsticePay Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (SolsticePay SRE), Priya Singh (SolsticePay CISO), Ethan Rowe (Product)

Summary: quick discovery focused on latency/throughput targets (p95), concurrency, streaming use cases and benchmarking approach. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC). Security questions around KMS and audit logs. Agreed next steps: share pricing & SOC2, schedule 1-week POC.

00:00 Jamie: hey everybody, thanks for joining, can you see my screen?
00:06 Maya: yep, all good, thanks.
00:10 Jamie: great. quick intro, I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood, ravi is our solutions eng, lena is cs. we're here to understand SolsticePay's latency and throughput goals and figure the right hosting mode, ok?
00:24 Ravi: hi all, I'll jump into the technical bits, particularly p95 targets and token/sec.
00:29 Ethan: hi, thx. we mainly ship real-time payments UX, so latency matters a lot.
00:35 Tom: and we have spikes during payroll windows, so concurrency and burst behavior are big concerns.
00:42 Priya: I'll focus on security/compliance, but interested in network isolation options.

01:05 Jamie: can you give us current baseline? what's your model and current infra?
01:11 Maya: sure. currently running a fine-tuned Llama2-13B on-prem for NLU routing and anti-fraud scoring. we get avg latencies around 180-250 ms for short prompts but p95 is spiky, closer to 700 ms under load. throughput at peak is roughly 350 requests per second with 1-2k token outputs.
01:33 Ravi: when you say requests, are those single-turn prompts or streaming responses?
01:36 Maya: mostly non-streaming for scoring, but product team wants streaming for the UX for chat-like flows.
01:42 Jamie: ok. so two primary patterns: short scoring (<256 tokens) and streaming long-form generation. got it.

02:00 Tom: our SRE is worried about cold-starts and model load times - we sometimes see 4-6 second slowdowns during autoscale.
02:08 Ravi: yeah that's typical if you don't have warm pools or pinned instances. Dedicated pools let you keep GPUs resident and reduce those cold starts.
02:15 Maya: can you summarize differences between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for latency?
02:20 Jamie: sure. Hosted gives fastest onboarding, but noisy neighbor can affect p95 - we provide latency SLOs for tiers; typical p95 for small models on hosted is 150-250 ms token generation for short sequences but depends on concurrency. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity with predictable p95 and lower variance - p95 reductions of 10-40% in some profiles. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control - lowest variability if you provision correctly, but you manage infra ops.

03:05 Ravi: also worth noting streaming behavior. with streaming we report latencies as initial token time (time-to-first-token) and per-token generation rate (tokens/sec). for many models we can do 30-120 tokens/sec depending on quantization and hardware.
03:22 Maya: 30-120 tokens/sec is a big range, what drives that?
03:26 Ravi: model size, quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit), GPU type (A100 vs H100 vs T4), batch size, and KV cache behavior. for 13B on A100 with 8-bit quant we typically see 60-80 tokens/sec single-request; on H100 with optimized kernels and fused attention can be 100+ tokens/sec.

04:00 Ethan: our p95 target for scoring is 200 ms end-to-end, including network and app processing. is that realistic with Hosted?
04:09 Jamie: it's tight but possible for short sequences if you pick the right model variant and route via the low-latency tier. we should validate with a POC. Hosted p95 under high concurrency can creep up if you hit multitenant limits. Dedicated gives more confidence.

05:00 Tom: concurrency - during payroll we expect sustained 5000 concurrent scoring requests for a 10-minute window, with spikes to 12k. what's Redwood's approach to autoscale and batching?
05:12 Ravi: our serving runtime supports continuous batching and dynamic batching with a policy per route; for Dedicated you can set reserved throughput and burst capacity. for 5k sustained, we'll look at sharding across multiples of the same model; token cost and batch efficiency will affect latency.
05:29 Maya: do you have empirical token/sec per GPU numbers?
05:33 Ravi: yes, for common stacks: Llama2-13B on A100 (40GB) 8-bit: ~60 tokens/sec single-stream; on H100 optimized: ~95-120 tokens/sec. For quantized 4-bit kernels you can push higher but depends on implementation. we'll share a spreadsheet with benchmark matrix.

06:10 Priya: security question: with Dedicated vs Hosted what about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs? we need customer-managed keys and full audit for PCI scope.
06:20 Jamie: Dedicated supports customer KMS via our key wrapping for model inputs/outputs in transit and at rest, and we can export audit logs to your SIEM. Private (VPC) gives you more control for PCI compliance; we also offer HSM integrations in our enterprise package.
06:34 Priya: and SSO/SAML and RBAC?
06:36 Lena: yes we support SAML2 SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based access controls per-route.

07:05 Maya: curious about p95 measurement methodology - do you use synthetic load or real-world traces during benchmarks?
07:11 Ravi: we prefer using a captured production trace if you can share anonymized traffic; otherwise we synthesize with distribution of prompt lengths, concurrency, and streaming vs non-streaming. we report p50/p95/p99 and token/sec and include cold-start percentiles.

08:00 Ethan: if we do Dedicated, what's typical lead time to provision reserved GPU pool?
08:06 Jamie: depends on region and capacity, usually 2-6 weeks, but we have accelerated options for higher commits.

09:00 Tom: cost - we need a sense of tokens/sec cost model vs latency tradeoff. can you show an example?
09:06 Jamie: yes, we'll send an example: hosted pay-as-you-go cost per token with autoscaling vs Dedicated monthly reserved capacity where unit cost per token goes down. we often model cost as tokens/sec * average token length * time, and show scenarios where Dedicated breaks even at X qps.

10:30 Maya: for the POC we want to target p95 <= 200ms for scoring (<=256 tokens) and streaming initial token <=150 ms and sustain >= 60 tokens/sec for the long-chat flows. is that achievable?
10:45 Ravi: scoring p95 200ms is feasible with Dedicated or high-priority Hosted if your model is 7B-13B and sequences are short. streaming initial token under 150ms and sustain 60 tokens/sec is feasible on A100 with proper quant and pinned instances. H100 would be more headroom.

12:00 Ethan: what about cold-start mitigation while autoscaling - can we keep a small warm pool?
12:05 Ravi: yes, you can configure minimum pool size and pre-warm policies. Dedicated typically gives pinned instances so cold-starts are negligible. Hosted has warm pools but not pinned.

14:15 Tom: do you provide client-side SDKs for streaming? latency for first byte matters and socket behavior sometimes adds 50-80ms.
14:22 Jamie: yes we have SDKs with streaming support and guidance on keep-alive and chunk sizes to minimize socket overhead. we'll share examples.

16:00 Maya: any limitations around token length and KV cache for conversational contexts?
16:05 Ravi: KV cache scales with sequence length; for long histories we recommend context window tuning and prefix caching. that affects memory and per-token throughput.

18:30 Priya: if we go Private (VPC), who manages patching and kernel updates for the runtime?
18:36 Jamie: Private deployments can be either customer-managed where you handle infra and we provide the control plane, or fully managed by Redwood under an enterprise SLA. patch cadence and maintenance windows are agreed in the contract.

20:00 Ethan: what telemetry can we get during the POC? we want per-route p95, token/sec, cost estimates, and traces.
20:08 Lena: Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route latency heatmaps, and trace hooks. we can provide a demo dashboard export for your team.

22:40 Maya: ok let's talk about the POC specifics - we want to run a 1-week performance POC with our anonymized production trace and a 50k request/day load with payroll-style spikes.
22:55 Ravi: that's doable. plan: first day ingest trace and set baseline; days 2-3 run hosted baseline; days 4-6 run Dedicated config(s) and compare p95, tokens/sec, and cost; day 7 review results and next steps.

25:10 Tom: during spikes we want graceful degradation not hard failures - do you support fallback to smaller models automatically?
25:17 Ravi: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible smaller variants and we have automatic fallback policies to keep requests served, alerting on quality regressions.

27:00 Maya: edge-case - we have latency SLO of 200ms p95 end-to-end; if hosting adds 40-60ms network, we need the model generation p95 <=140-160ms. can you target that?
27:12 Ravi: it's tight, but with Dedicated pinned instances, batching tuned to small windows, and an optimized kernel path we can often hit generation p95 ~130-160ms for short prompts on H100; A100 might be closer to 160-200 depending on quant. we'll validate in POC.

30:00 Ethan: any gotchas for tokenization differences affecting token/sec?
30:05 Ravi: yes tokenization affects token counts and therefore tokens/sec; we recommend normalizing tokenization in the benchmark to match production. small changes can change throughput numbers by 5-10%.

32:00 Priya: for PCI audit, can we get proof of key management and how logs are stored?
32:06 Jamie: yes we'll attach our SOC2 and addendums for KMS/HSM, show encryption at rest, and audit log retention policies.

34:40 Maya: do you have switching latency if we want canary between models during rollouts?
34:45 Ravi: rollouts are supported with canaries and A/B; switching latency depends on whether the variant is warmed. we recommend warming steps as part of rollout.

36:30 Tom: one more on autoscale - if we need burst to 12k concurrent, do you recommend Dedicated with burst capacity or hybrid approach?
36:37 Jamie: Dedicated with configured burst capacity is best for predictable spikes; hybrid routing (primary Dedicated + fallback to Hosted) gives extra headroom during extreme spikes but watch for p95 differences.

38:10 Ethan: ok, what's the expected data we should share to start the POC?
38:15 Maya: we'll provide anonymized traces, token distribution, and a list of critical prompts.
38:22 Priya: and a security req doc.

40:00 Ravi: perfect. we'll draft a POC plan and benchmark matrix: p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-token, sustained tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, cold-start percentiles, and error rates.

42:20 Jamie: recap - SolsticePay wants p95 <=200ms scoring, initial token <=150ms for streaming, sustain >=60 tokens/sec. next steps: we (Redwood) send pricing, SOC2 docs, benchmark spreadsheet; schedule 1-week POC week of Sep 20; Priya to send security questionnaire; Maya to share anonymized trace.

44:05 Maya: sounds good. one nit - please include model versioning and quantization recommendations in the plan.
44:12 Ravi: will do, we'll include 8-bit vs 4-bit recommendations and expected token/sec deltas.

46:00 Tom: ok thanks, any final Qs?
46:03 Priya: none from me.
46:05 Ethan: all good.

46:30 Jamie: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the docs and set the POC kickoff.
46:36 Lena: I'll send calendar invites after Jamie shares proposed dates.

49:00 Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors and mis-hearings ("Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated in a few spots, "KV cash" for KV cache). References to benchmarks/spreadsheets and SOC2 docs will be shared via email/link.
